parts.label: a
parts.technique: Finding an unknown sum from a given mean
parts.reason: S2.3 covers mean/variance calculation including from summary statistics; finding t from mean=Σx/n is basic use of summary statistics, not excluded.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Variance from summary statistics (Sxx formula)
parts.reason: S2.3 explicitly covers calculation of standard deviation/variance from summary statistics using Sxx.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Interpreting variance to identify source class
parts.reason: S2.3 explicitly expects students to draw inferences and interpretations from measures of variation.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Combining summary statistics for a merged data set to find mean and variance
parts.reason: S2.3 covers mean and variance calculation from summary statistics; combining two data sets uses the same Sxx-based approach, no excluded method required.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Effect of linear coding on mean and variance
parts.reason: S2.3 guidance explicitly states 'Understanding and use of coding' as part of the section.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Venn diagram representation of union
parts.reason: S3.2 explicitly covers use of Venn diagrams for events.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Mutually exclusive events probability rules
parts.reason: S3.1 covers mutually exclusive events and calculating probabilities using addition rule (P(A∪B) in S3.2).

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Independent events probability rules
parts.reason: S3.1 explicitly covers independent events including P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B) and the addition formula in S3.2.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Interpreting PMCC value for linear relationship
parts.reason: S5.1 permits interpreting a given/calculated correlation coefficient value (calculation via formula excluded, but interpretation of a value close to -1 supporting linearity is explicitly allowed).

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Definition of response variable
parts.reason: S2.2 explicitly covers the terms explanatory (independent) and response (dependent) variables.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Calculating gradient of regression line from Sxy/Sxx to test a claim
parts.reason: S2.2 explicit exclusion: 'calculations involving regression lines are excluded'; this part requires computing the regression gradient.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Calculating regression line intercept to estimate a value
parts.reason: S2.2 explicit exclusion: 'calculations involving regression lines are excluded'; this part computes the intercept and predicts a value using the regression equation.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Expectation of a discrete random variable
parts.reason: S4.1 explicit exclusion: 'calculation of mean and variance of discrete random variables is excluded'.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Using E(X) and Var(X)=E(X^2) to find unknown probabilities
parts.reason: S4.1 explicit exclusion of mean/variance calculation for discrete random variables; this part requires E(X) and E(X^2).

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Var(aX+b) for a discrete random variable
parts.reason: S4.1 explicit exclusion of variance calculation for discrete random variables.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Probabilities for a transformed discrete random variable Y=1-X
parts.reason: This part relies on the values of a and b found in part (b), which is out-of-spec (S4.1 exclusion); per the rule, a part depending on an out-of-spec answer is OUT.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Substitution into a linear coding relationship
parts.reason: S2.3 guidance explicitly includes 'understanding and use of coding'; recovering the original value from a coded value w via x=1000w+20000 is a straightforward coding substitution, not a regression/correlation calculation, so the S2.2/S5.1 exclusions do not apply here.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Calculating the PMCC using the formula
parts.reason: S5.1 explicit exclusion: 'calculation of correlation coefficients is excluded' / 'use of the formula is not required'; this part requires deriving r via Swy/Sww/Syy formula.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Effect of coding on correlation coefficient
parts.reason: This part is about stating the correlation coefficient value between x and y based on the excluded PMCC calculation in (b); tied to an out-of-spec calculation, so treated as OUT.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Converting a regression line under coding to obtain regression line of y on x
parts.reason: S2.2 explicit exclusion: 'calculations involving regression lines are excluded'.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Using a regression line to estimate a response value
parts.reason: S2.2 explicit exclusion of regression line calculations; also depends on out-of-spec part (d).

parts.label: f
parts.technique: Assessing reliability of estimates (interpolation/extrapolation) from a regression line
parts.reason: Although S2.2 guidance mentions interpolation/extrapolation conceptually, this part only makes sense after the excluded regression-line calculations in (d)/(e), so per the rule it is OUT.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Probability without replacement using complement
parts.reason: S3.2 covers conditional/sequential probability with tree diagrams and complement rule P(A')=1-P(A).

parts.label: c

parts.reason: S3.2 covers use of tree diagrams for dependent/conditional probability.

parts.reason: S3.2 explicitly gives and requires use of the conditional probability formula P(A|B)=P(A∩B)/P(B).

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Probability of an ordered sequence without replacement
parts.reason: S3.2 covers use of tree diagrams for sequences of dependent events.
